question: Does outbound link tracking count clicks on mailto: links on my contact page? If not, how can I track them?
reference_answer: No. Email (`mailto:`) and phone (`tel:`) links don't lead to a website, so outbound link tracking doesn't count them. You can track them as custom events either by adding a CSS class to each link or by adding a script that tracks all email and phone links automatically, but pick only one so clicks aren't counted twice.

Use one method, not both, or clicks are counted twice

Add a script to your pages to track all email and phone links automatically [1]. After choosing a method, you must add the corresponding goal in your site settings under the Goals section [1].

evidence.title: Track clicks on email and phone links
evidence.text: Note: If you track link clicks, then these count towards your billable monthly pageviews. Outbound link tracking counts clicks on links to other websites. Email links (`mailto:`) and phone links (`tel:`) don't lead to a website, so they aren't counted there. You can track them as custom events in one of two ways. Pick one, not both, or each click is counted twice. ## Option 1: Tag the links you want to track Add a CSS class to each email or phone link, the same way as for any custom event with CSS class names: ```html Email us Call us ``` This works well when you only have a few such links, and you can tag them from most site builders and CMSs without touching code. ## Option 2: Track every email and phone link automatically Add this script to every page, right below your Plausible snippet: ```html ``` It catches clicks on all email and phone links on the page, including ones you add later, and sends the address that was clicked as the `url` property. ## Add the goals in your site settings Go to your site settings, open **Goals**, click **+ Add goal**, choose **Custom event** and add the event names you used: `Email Link Click` and `Phone Link Click` for option 1, or `Email Link: Click` and `Phone Link: Click` for option 2.

evidence.title: Adding Plausible to Carrd
evidence.text:
Here's how to add Plausible Analytics to your Carrd site and set up the tracking of custom events such as button clicks.

### Get your site snippet

We display your snippet during the process of adding a new site to your account. You can also see the snippet within the **Site Installation** area of the **General** section in your site settings.

### Go to your Carrd website editor

* Go to the editor of your Carrd website and add an **Embed** component.

Add embed element to Carrd

* In the element's settings make sure:

- Type is set to **Code**
- Style is set to **Hidden** and **Head**

* Then paste your Plausible tracking script in the **Code** field

* In your copied snippet, set `hashBasedRouting` to `true` in the `plausible.init()` call. Keep the rest of your snippet, including its site-specific script URL, unchanged:

```js
plausible.init({ hashBasedRouting: true });
```

If your `plausible.init()` call already contains other options, keep them and add `hashBasedRouting: true`. This allows Plausible to track hashed page paths that Carrd uses during navigation.

* Do click on the **Done** button and then **Publish** your changes. After you change the tracking snippet on your site, all the hash-based page paths on your Carrd website will start being tracked and will be displayed in the **Top Pages** tab of your Plausible Analytics dashboard.

Now you can go to your Carrd website and verify that Plausible script has been added and to your Plausible account to see whether the stats are being tracked. See here how to verify the integration.

question: can i see my plausible dashboard inside odoo? i made a shared link with a password but odoo wont show it
reference_answer: Odoo's embedded dashboard does not support password protection, so create the shared link in Settings > Visibility with password protection off. Then in Odoo enable Plausible Analytics under Website > Configuration > Settings, paste the link into Shared Link Auth and save.

Then, in Odoo, go to Website → Configuration → Settings, enable Plausible Analytics, paste your shared link into the Shared Link Auth field, and save [1].

evidence.title: Plausible pricing and subscription plans
evidence.text:
Plausible gives you full control over your subscription. Choose a plan, pick monthly or yearly billing and upgrade or downgrade as your needs change. No long-term contracts.

## Which plan should I choose?

All plans start at the same pageview tiers. The difference is features and team size.

- **Starter**: one site, solo use, no team or sharing needed
- **Growth**: multiple sites, or need to invite team members, share dashboards with clients or save site segments and site notes for the whole team
- **Business**: need funnels, user journeys, revenue tracking, custom properties, a consolidated view of several sites, Stats API or Data Studio (build custom dashboards and blend Plausible data with other sources like ad spend or CRM data)
- **Enterprise**: large scale, SSO, Sites API, managed proxy or raw data exports. Contact us to discuss

Compare full features and pricing on our website or in the **Subscription** section of your settings. Save 2 months by choosing yearly billing.

All plans include a 30-day free trial, no credit card required. During the trial you have access to all Business plan features and limits, so you can explore the full product before choosing a plan.

Not sure which plan fits? When you choose a plan in your account, the page shows your billable pageviews over the last 30 days, selects the pageview tier that covers them and marks the plan that fits your usage and the features you've been using as **Recommended**. On a trial, it's worth checking near the end, once it covers a full month of your traffic.

Our 15% discount is available only to nonprofits, educational institutions and open-source projects. It applies to Business plans with annual billing only. See nonprofit and education pricing for eligibility and how to apply.

question: we use cookiebot with automatic blocking and plausible isnt counting people who havent accepted the banner yet. how do i let plausible load anyway?
reference_answer: With Cookiebot's automatic cookie blocking, add the data-cookieconsent="ignore" attribute to the Plausible script tag. If your visit still doesn't show in realtime, add the same attribute to the short inline script that follows it too.
key_facts: Add data-cookieconsent="ignore" to the Plausible script tag
If needed, add it to the inline script that follows as well
answer: To allow Plausible to load while using Cookiebot with automatic blocking, add the `data-cookieconsent="ignore"` attribute to the Plausible script tag [1]. If your visit still does not appear in the realtime view, add the same attribute to the short inline script that follows it in your snippet [1]. You should only add this attribute when needed, as Cookiebot advises against adding it to scripts it would not otherwise block [1].

evidence.title: Use Plausible alongside a consent management platform
evidence.text:
When Cookiebot runs with automatic cookie blocking, add the `data-cookieconsent="ignore"` attribute to the Plausible script tag:

```html
<script data-cookieconsent="ignore" async src="https://plausible.io/js/pa-XXXXX.js"></script>
```

If your visit still doesn't show up in the realtime view after that, add the same attribute to the short inline script that follows it in your snippet too. Cookiebot advises against adding it to scripts it wouldn't block, so add it there only when needed.

Use the script URL from your own snippet (**Site Settings → General → Site Installation**). In Cookiebot's manual blocking mode, scripts only wait for consent when you mark them, so leave the Plausible snippet as it is. More in Cookiebot's guide.

evidence.title: Adding Plausible to Ghost
evidence.text:
You can use the **Ghost code injection** feature to add Plausible Analytics tracking code to your Ghost website same way you would add Google Analytics code or any other JavaScript code.

In Ghost you can inject code across your entire site or on an individual post or page. Since Plausible needs to track analytics across your entire site, use the global code injection feature which can be found in the Ghost Admin settings menu.

* In Ghost Admin, open **Settings → Advanced → Code Injection**. You can also follow Ghost's current code injection guide.

* Paste your Plausible tracking snippet to the **Site Header** text box. Code added into the **Site Header** field is injected into the `<head>` tag on every page of your site.

* After adding your code, click on the **Save** button.

Now you can go to your website and verify whether Plausible Analytics script has been added and to your Plausible Analytics account to see whether the stats are being tracked. See here how to verify the integration.

Ghost Portal flows

The Sign In/Sign up flows are part of Ghost's Portal app and it's an unified experience for all Ghost sites. You cannot customize these flows by adding an ID or CSS class.

However, you can bypass this and customize your sign up flows by using a custom theme on the "Creator plan" or higher.

If you're using a custom theme, you can keep your Plausible tracking snippet installed and add the event CSS class to the element that you want to track as explained in this doc.

- Invite your team or create a shared link for collaborators who need read access to your stats
